objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger.
chief_complaint: Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger

fragments.text: The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.
Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist
Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint
Extended right ring finger in resting position
Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

exam_leaves.text: Right ring finger is extended, with visible swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint.
Tenderness localized at the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.
Patient unable to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint while attempting to make a fist. No joint laxity.
Normal capillary refill, no sensory deficits.

test_leaves.text: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.
Expected to show details regarding the integrity of tendons.

correct_diagnosis: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
